turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that and on what basis.
Don't thank me. I'm waiting for a name, Hale.
The file was created at 11:31 PM. 612 words appeared at 11:52 PM and 794 more at 11:58 PM.

"11:31 PM," and on what day, Hale? You haven't said, and I'm not taking times off a screen I can't see, so turn it around and show me. And you still haven't told me who decided the zero, or whether anyone asked Owen before it went in.
How long after the file was created did the first words appear?
You're leading me, Hale, and I've done this for twenty years. Do your own arithmetic. I asked you for a date and a name, and I'm still waiting on both.
What time is it now, by the way?
Near enough twenty past four, which leaves you twenty minutes before my call. Spend them on the date of that file and on who entered the zero.
